renderer_reuse_stop.finding: Top-level FramePacket upload/copy/task/custom-callback counts do not cover content effects encoded inside RenderPass. The existing source proves these paths exist, but does not prove that every ordinary gameplay frame necessarily depends on them.
renderer_reuse_stop.reason: A fail-closed second-frame gate needs to classify persistent RenderPass targets and callbacks, including cached/offscreen and resolved textures. A gate that merely rejects every RenderPass would be vacuous for the drawn component; allowing ordinary EFB output based only on queue-write completion or the packet reset would guess that no next-tick consumer exists. Establishing reusable target/resource lineage would exceed the bounded smallest_B_contract. Per root instruction, stopped before creating a vacuous gate or broad redesign.

source_paths.fact: paletteConvs encode before the discardable-pass early return, so a discardable RenderPass is not evidence of no GPU content effect.
RenderPass color/depth attachment load/clear/store behavior and resolve views are encoded. Load may consume prior target content.
The encoder can add a depth snapshot, resolveTarget conversion/blit/copy, and color/depth snapshot copies outside the top-level FrameOp TextureCopy list.

EFB can be suspended while cached offscreen textures are acquired and rendered; restore resumes the EFB, and frame-local pass metadata alone does not prove whether a cached output is consumed next tick.
resolve_pass_into records a resolveTarget and resumes EFB; resolve_pass may create cached color/depth snapshot destinations and resumes EFB with load semantics.
Discard finalization writes browser staging prefixes, moves callbacks, resets the CPU FramePacket, and does not finish or submit the encoder. Resetting the packet is not GPU-target/cache rollback.
The private match-draw discard lifecycle remains deliberately one-shot; relaxing it is not part of this candidate.

scope.conclusion: No second-frame renderer admission is established by existing reset semantics or current terminal evidence. This is an unclassified ownership blocker, not proof that a second frame is impossible or too slow. Seven-tick component execution remains unrun.

Then design one compact fail-closed receipt and a real end-to-begin runtime control that exceeds active frame-slot count, verifies packet/high-water reset and exactly-once lease return, and injects one known unsafe content operation. Preserve one-shot behavior.
